role: museum furniture — a closed oak cabinet giving human scale and somewhere for relics to live
note: Multi-image conditioning, NOT text. This request has no prompt field: the turnaround views carry the entire style, so the brief and the anchor image are part of this asset's provenance.

curation.purpose: Fourth kit module. Straightforward solid furniture, included because a room of nothing but wall fittings still has no furniture in it.

reject: Doors glazed, transparent, or open — the brief specifies solid panelled oak.
Carcass reads as a flat slab with no depth or plinth.
Doors not distinguishable as two leaves with a central stile.
Any lettering, numerals, or invented inscription.
Sits implausibly — proportions that cannot stand.
accept: One closed cabinet: rectangular carcass on a plinth base with a projecting cornice.
Two full-height doors divided into panels by raised mouldings, with a central stile.
Brass ring pulls and visible hinges.
Solid opaque panelled oak with visible grain; no glass anywhere.
Wider across the front than it is deep.

placement.note: Angled against the wall clear of the exhibit. Its joinery is what has to survive reconstruction; the brass pulls are the detail that tells you whether the texture pass worked.

viewSelection: Sheet 1536x1024, magenta background as briefed. Two views, trimmed 649x919 and 627x979 — genuinely different angles. Keyed only 4.9% and 6.9%, consistent with a closed solid body having no hole to key.
